tldr: Headlines converge on a single factual anchor — Russia struck both of Kyiv's major Dnipro bridges within three days — with most outlets naming specific bridges and sequencing the attacks; secondary tiers stress transport disruption or civilian casualties, while TASS alone frames the bridges as military supply conduits rather than civilian crossings.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Uses Russian-transliterated place names ('Kiev', 'Dnieper') and characterises the bridge solely as a military troop-transfer route — the only headline in the cluster to omit civilian or commuter context entirely.

The only headline to frame the event as a bilateral exchange ('Russia, Ukraine exchange overnight strikes') rather than a unilateral Russian escalation, pairing the bridge attack with Ukrainian counter-strikes on Russia's Kaluga region.
Leads with fatalities and pivots to energy-facility targeting — the only headline to sideline the bridge story in favour of a broader overnight-strike casualty and energy-infrastructure narrative.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents near-universal factual consensus on Russian bridge strikes in Kyiv but splits on emphasis: most outlets frame a security escalation, Politico and Malay Mail lead with logistics disruption, and TASS uniquely markets the targeted Dnipro crossings as military supply infrastructure rather than a civilian capital's arteries.
